$comment: Source of truth for the standards catalog. Rules are web adaptations written in our own words, informed by Apple's Human Interface Guidelines; no HIG prose is copied. STANDARDS.md is generated from this file: run `npm run catalog:docs`.
units: 1 HIG pt = 1 CSS px, written in rem at a 16 px root unless the rule says px. The CSS pt unit is banned (LIB-01).

standards.rule: Put the most important content first in reading order (top, then the inline-start side). DOM order matches visual order.
standards.threshold: No `tabindex>0`. No CSS `order` or `*-reverse` on interactive siblings.

standards.rule: Align items to a shared grid. Indentation shows subordination. Group related items with spacing, containers, or separators.
Use progressive disclosure for secondary detail (accordion, menu, "more" page) rather than showing everything.
Adapt to available space (container or viewport width), never to user-agent or device type.
Functionality is identical at every width. Only how much is visible, and how it is arranged, changes (e.g., nav links ↔ drawer, sidebar filters ↔ filter sheet).
standards.threshold: Key flows pass at 320 px and 1280 px

standards.rule: Reflow: vertical content never needs two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px width.
Layout survives large text: adjacent items stack, containers grow, nothing clips or overlaps.
standards.threshold: 200% root font-size: no clipped text, no horizontal scroll

standards.rule: Respect safe areas. With `viewport-fit=cover`, backgrounds bleed edge to edge while controls sit inside `env(safe-area-inset-*)`.
standards.threshold: Fixed and sticky bars pad by `env()`

standards.rule: Constrain prose to a readable measure.
Full-bleed media fills its frame without distortion: scale or crop (`object-fit: cover`), never stretch.
standards.threshold: No `object-fit: fill` on media with mismatched ratio

standards.rule: Fixed or sticky chrome (header, bottom cart bar) never fully hides the focused element or critical controls.
standards.threshold: Focused element at least partly visible; `scroll-padding` set

standards.rule: Use size classes: compact / regular / wide breakpoints at page level, container queries inside components.
RTL-ready: logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `text-align: start`), so `dir="rtl"` mirrors the layout.
RTL exceptions: don't mirror numerals, logos, photos, media controls that point to real directions, or real-world objects. Do mirror back/forward chevrons, progress, and text-direction icons.
Default reading text is the Body style. No rendered text is smaller than the minimum.
standards.threshold: Body 17 px (1.0625rem); min 11 px anywhere; storefront legal or meta text ≥ 12 px (ours)

standards.rule: Font sizes use `rem`/`em` so browser text-size settings scale them (the Dynamic Type analogue). Never set the root font-size in px.
standards.threshold: Stylelint: `font-size` units ∈ {rem, em, %}; `html` font-size not px

standards.rule: Text enlarges to at least 200% with no loss of content or function.
No light weights for UI text. Use regular, semibold, or bold only. A thin display face needs larger sizes.
Hierarchy comes from a fixed set of text styles (Large Title … Caption 2, plus 2 display sizes). No ad-hoc sizes.
Minimise typefaces.
standards.threshold: ≤ 2 families per page (sans + optional serif/display); mono only in code, SKUs, and numbers
standards.note: Revised from the research report for the owner decision of 2026-11-03: open fonts only (Inter, Source Serif 4, IBM Plex Mono; all OFL-1.1), no SF Pro.

standards.rule: Leading suits the use: tight for single-line UI, loose for long passages. Never tight leading on 3+ lines.
User text-spacing overrides cause no clipping or overlap.
standards.threshold: Inject line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em; no overflow clip

standards.rule: Minimise truncation as text grows. Important text (product titles, prices, errors) wraps. Any truncated text is available in full on the same or the next view.
standards.threshold: Clamp ≤ 3 lines on cards; full text on PDP

standards.rule: At large text sizes, drop columns and stack secondary items (badges, prices, timestamps) under the text.
Keep hierarchy order stable as text grows (primary items stay first and on top).

Font delivery: open (OFL-1.1) fonts only. Inter for UI and body text, Source Serif 4 for optional editorial headings, IBM Plex Mono for code and numbers. No SF Pro, not even through system-font keywords; never ship Apple font files (§3.1).
standards.threshold: Asset scan rejects `SF-*`, `SFNS*`, `SFPro*`, `NewYork*`; `@font-face` must not name SF; font stacks do not name `-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, or SF fonts
standards.note: Revised from the research report for the owner decision of 2026-11-03: open fonts only (Inter, Source Serif 4, IBM Plex Mono; all OFL-1.1), no SF Pro.

standards.rule: Custom (web) fonts still honour user text size; use `font-display: swap` and metric-matched fallbacks to avoid layout shift.
Text contrast meets the minimum against its actual background, in every appearance mode.
standards.threshold: 4.5:1; 3:1 for large text (≥ 24 px, or ≥ 18.66 px bold) (LIB-04)

standards.rule: Primary and secondary text roles aim higher, as HIG dark-mode guidance asks for custom colors.
Component boundaries, focus indicators, and meaningful icons contrast with adjacent colors.
Never use color alone for meaning (sale price, error, stock state, selected swatch, link in text). Add text, an icon, a shape, or an underline.
One meaning per color. Accent means interactive / primary action, so non-interactive text never uses the accent or link color.
Components use semantic role tokens only (`bg`, `label`, `separator`, `link`, `accent`, `status-*`) and never repurpose a role (e.g., separator as text).
standards.threshold: Stylelint: no hex/rgb/hsl/named colors outside the tokens build

standards.rule: Every color role defines four values: light, dark, increased-contrast light, increased-contrast dark.
Use accent sparingly: at most 1–2 filled-accent (prominent) buttons per view.
Over colourful content (hero images, colored sections), controls go monochrome rather than adding accent-coloured labels.
Images use or embed sRGB. P3 is optional, gated by `@media (color-gamut: p3)` with an sRGB fallback.
Don't hard-code Apple system color values. They are reference only; tokens are our own.
Status colors are consistent site-wide, and their cultural meaning is reviewed (red is not universally "danger").
Follow the OS appearance (`prefers-color-scheme`) and declare `color-scheme: light dark`. Any site toggle defaults to "System" (LIB-15).
A dark palette is designed, not inverted: dimmer backgrounds, brighter foregrounds, base vs elevated surfaces. Sheets, popovers, and dialogs use elevated.
standards.threshold: Token test: luminance of elevated > base in dark

standards.rule: Check contrast in light, dark, and both increased-contrast modes.
standards.threshold: axe run in every color project

standards.rule: Soften white-background product images in dark mode so they don't glow.
Icons work in both appearances. SVG icons use `currentColor`; raster logos get dark variants.
standards.threshold: Lint: SVG icons have no hard-coded fill

standards.rule: Native form controls follow the scheme through `color-scheme`; custom fields use role tokens.
Touch and click targets meet the default control size. The WCAG minimum is an absolute floor for dense inline cases.
standards.threshold: Default ≥ 44×44 px; floor 24×24 px with spacing exception

standards.rule: Space between targets matters as much as size.
standards.threshold: ~12 px around bezeled controls, ~24 px around borderless ones

standards.rule: Every control has an accessible name; icon-only buttons have labels; the visible label is part of the name.
Meaningful images get alt text; decorative images get `alt=""` or `aria-hidden`.
Headings and landmarks give structure: one `h1`, no skipped levels, header/nav/main/footer.
Announce dynamic changes (cart count, add-to-cart result, filter result counts) through a live region.
Everything works by keyboard alone, including dropdown/mega navigation. No keyboard traps.
standards.threshold: Playwright Tab walk reaches every interactive element; Esc closes overlays

standards.rule: Don't override browser or OS shortcuts. Custom shortcuts only for frequent commands, never single-character without a modifier.
Every focusable element shows a visible focus indicator.
standards.threshold: `:focus-visible` outline ≥ 2 px, ≥ 3:1 vs unfocused state and adjacent color

standards.rule: Focus never moves without user action. Focus order follows DOM order. Only a dedicated search page may autofocus its field.
Sticky headers and bars never fully obscure focus.
Every gesture (swipe carousel, drag slider, swipe-to-dismiss sheet) has a single-pointer, button-based alternative.
No time-boxed UI for essential information. Toasts carrying errors or actions persist until dismissed.
standards.threshold: No auto-dismiss on `role=alert` or toasts with actions

standards.rule: Media is under the user's control: no autoplay with sound; autoplaying motion has a pause control; captions on spoken video.
standards.threshold: `video[autoplay]` must be `muted` with a pause control; `<track kind=captions>` on spoken video

standards.rule: No flashing content.
Declare the page language and the language of foreign-language passages.
Forced colors (Windows contrast themes): no information lost, focus still visible.
Respect `prefers-contrast: more` by switching to the increased-contrast token set.
Charts, size guides, and infographics also expose their data as text or a table.
Motion is purposeful and brief. Durations and easings come from tokens.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, replace translate/scale/zoom/parallax with fades or nothing. No depth or blur animation. Carousels don't auto-advance.
standards.threshold: `document.getAnimations()` has no transform keyframes under reduce

standards.rule: Motion never carries information alone; pair it with a text or state change.
Motion is interruptible; nothing blocks input while it plays.
No decorative motion on high-frequency interactions (e.g., scaling every product card on hover).
Feedback motion follows the spatial model: a sheet that rises from the bottom dismisses downward; a side drawer exits to its side.
Auto-advancing content (carousels, tickers) is off by default; when on, it has pause/stop.
standards.threshold: Applies if it runs > 5 s; `marquee` and `blink` banned (axe)

standards.rule: Translucent "glass" material only for the functional layer floating above content (sticky header, bottom bar, sheet chrome), never for content cards.
Use material sparingly, on the most important functional surfaces only.
Text on material stays legible against the worst-case backdrop.
standards.threshold: Token test: label and secondary label ≥ 4.5:1 with the material composited over pure black and pure white (§4.3)

standards.rule: Fallbacks: no `backdrop-filter` → opaque; `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` → opaque; `prefers-contrast: more` → opaque + border; `forced-colors` → `Canvas`.
"Clear" (very transparent) material only over media, with a dark scrim when the media is bright.
Elevation: light mode uses a shadow scale; dark mode uses lighter elevated surfaces plus a hairline border instead of shadows.
Pick a material by role (thin/regular/thick), not by look. Thicker material for dense text.
One scroll-edge treatment (fade or blur) per view where content scrolls under floating chrome.
Interface icons are simple and consistent (grid, stroke, corner style), with stroke weight matched to adjacent text.
standards.threshold: One icon set per site; stroke token

standards.rule: Icons are SVG, use `currentColor`, and are sized in `em`/tokens so they scale with text.
Icon-only controls carry a text alternative; decorative icons are `aria-hidden="true"`.
standards.threshold: axe + custom: an `svg` in a nameless button fails

standards.rule: Familiar actions get familiar icons (search, cart, account, close, share, wishlist). Use a text label when it reads clearer.
Provide a selected-state icon variant only when needed (filled heart), and expose state via `aria-pressed`.
No SF Symbols or confusingly similar glyphs; no renderings of Apple hardware (§3.1).
Avoid text inside icons; localize any icon that must contain text.
RTL mirroring per LAY-14.
Serve resolution-appropriate images (1×–3× DPR) through `srcset`/`sizes` (Shopify `image_url` + `image_tag`).
Photos as JPEG/WebP/AVIF; flat art and icons as SVG; PNG only for raster art that needs transparency.
Images are sRGB (or tagged); check them on real devices.
Text over images gets guaranteed contrast from a scrim/overlay token, never from the image itself.
standards.threshold: Overlay token required on text-over-media components

standards.rule: Show media at its original aspect ratio and reserve its space.
Imagery and copy are inclusive (people, settings, no stereotypes).
Same as ACC-01: the hit region meets the default size even when the visible shape is smaller.
Custom buttons have distinct hover, pressed (`:active`), `:focus-visible`, and disabled states.
At most one prominent (filled accent) button per section, and at most two per view.
Mark the preferred option by style (filled / tinted / plain), not by size. Buttons in a set share a size.
Labels are verbs ("Add to cart", "Check out"). No "click here". Sentence-style capitalisation, no trailing punctuation.
Roles are primary, cancel, and destructive. A destructive action is never the primary/default (Enter) button; it is styled as destructive.
Slow actions show progress inside the button, with an updated label ("Adding…") and `aria-busy`. The button keeps its size, and the result is announced.
An action that needs more input before it completes ends its label with "…" ("Choose options…").

Apple Pay / express checkout: never build or imitate Apple Pay buttons; use Shopify's dynamic checkout rendering. Platform buttons are never smaller or harder to reach than other payment buttons. Side by side, Apple Pay sits after "Add to cart", with a matching corner radius.
standards.threshold: No "Apple Pay" strings or logos in theme assets

standards.rule: Every field has a persistent visible label. Placeholder text is only a hint or example.
standards.threshold: axe `label`; custom: a placeholder is never the only label

standards.rule: Use the right `type`/`inputmode`/`autocomplete` (email, tel, postal-code, `cc-*`) so the correct keyboard and autofill appear. Get data from the system (autofill) rather than retyping.
standards.threshold: Known-purpose fields carry an `autocomplete` token; axe `autocomplete-valid`

standards.rule: Field width hints at the expected length.
Validate at the right time: format on blur, password rules before leaving the field. Errors sit next to the field, are linked by `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid`.
Error copy says how to fix the problem; no blame, no "Oops", no bare "Invalid X".
Never prefill passwords. Use secure fields with show/hide, and support password managers and passkeys.
Offer choices instead of typing where possible (select, radios, segmented, stepper).
Mark required data clearly. Keep submit enabled; validate on submit and focus the first error (LIB-16).
Don't ask for the same data twice in a flow (e.g., billing defaults to shipping).
Switches only in list/settings rows. Elsewhere use a toggle button (`aria-pressed`) or checkbox. State is never shown by color alone.
Radios for mutually exclusive options beyond two; a checkbox for a single on/off; select/picker for medium-to-long lists in logical order.
Segmented controls (e.g., variant options): few segments of consistent width, either text or icons (not mixed), with noun labels.
A quantity stepper shows the value it changes and pairs with an editable number field. Min/max are enforced and changes announced.
Range sliders (price filter) pair with number inputs and use the familiar direction (min at the start), mirrored in RTL.
Search: placeholder says what is searched; results refine as the user types (debounced); suggestions; clear button; filters default broad.
Tabbing between fields follows the visual order.
Show search history only with privacy in mind (clearable, local).
Primary navigation is for navigating, not for actions. It stays visible and consistent across sections.
Keep top-level destinations few, with no overflow "More" bucket; single-word labels where possible.
Never hide or disable a navigation item because its content is empty; show an empty state instead.
Nav items have text labels. The current location is marked.
Badges only for actionable or critical info (cart count), with accessible text ("Cart, 3 items").
standards.threshold: Badge text in the accessible name

standards.rule: Sidebars and menus show at most two hierarchy levels; deeper content gets its own page.
Sidebar (filters/collections) on wide layouts ↔ sheet/drawer on compact, with identical functionality.
Give search a prominent position when it matters (header at all widths, and a dedicated results page).
Standard back/close affordances. Breadcrumbs for deep catalogs (web extension).
Header/toolbar is not overcrowded. Group by function: leading (logo, menu), center, trailing (search, account, cart). Trailing items stay visible at all widths.
Page titles are unique and concise, and don't lead with the store name.
Carousel page indicators only for short sets; longer sets use thumbnails or a grid.
Skip link to main content (web extension).
Use modality only when it clearly helps. Keep modal tasks short, with no navigation stacks inside a modal.
One modal at a time. Close the first before opening another, and never stack two alerts.
Obvious dismissal: visible Close, Esc, backdrop/swipe for sheets. Focus returns to the element that opened the modal.
Confirm before closing a modal that would discard user input.
Each modal is titled with its task.
Sheets (cart drawer, filters) pair Done/Apply with Cancel or Back. Resizable sheets show a grabber. Swipe-to-dismiss on touch, plus a button.
Long or complex flows get a page, not a sheet.
Popovers (menus, previews): small content, one at a time, anchored to their trigger, never for warnings. On compact widths they become sheets.
standards.threshold: Popover → sheet below the compact breakpoint

standards.rule: Alerts are rare and actionable. No alert for undoable actions (remove from cart → undo toast). Nothing modal opens on page load (no entry newsletter pop-ups; legal age/consent gates excepted).
standards.threshold: No dialog opens within 10 s of load without interaction

standards.rule: Alert copy: concise title, message only if useful. Buttons are 1–2 word verbs; "Cancel" cancels; "OK" only for purely informational alerts; no Yes/No.
Button order: the default action trails in a row (or tops a stack); Cancel leads (or sits at the bottom). Mirrored in RTL.
A destructive confirmation always offers Cancel. The destructive button looks destructive and is not the default.
Use action sheets for choices tied to an intentional action. Neither alerts nor action sheets should scroll.
Use native `<dialog>` (`showModal`) and the `popover` attribute; make the background inert.
Text-heavy data (orders, specs) as lists or tables; visual items (products) as grids.
Collections use the standard grid; cards in one grid share size and image ratio.
Items give press feedback. A product card has one primary link (single tab stop) with a visible focus ring.
Row and card text is succinct; long titles wrap within a line cap, with the full text available.
Tables have descriptive headers (`<th scope>`).
Insert/remove/reorder animation is subtle and respects reduced motion.
Avoid layout jumps from dynamic content (infinite scroll, lazy cards); reserve space.
No same-direction nested scroll containers (a horizontal rail inside the vertical page is fine).
Show that more content exists: horizontal rails let the next item peek.
Disclosures (`details`/`summary`) have descriptive labels; at most one "show more" disclosure button per view.
Show something immediately. Skeletons and placeholders reserve the layout.
People keep browsing while things load (async add-to-cart and filters).
Determinate progress when the length is known, a spinner only otherwise. Keep it moving, in a consistent place.
Feedback is multimodal: text + icon + color, announced via a live region.
Status sits next to the thing it describes (inline stock, inline errors), not in a global alert.
Warn only for unexpected, irreversible loss. Expected removals get undo instead of a warning.
Confirm significant completions (added to cart, order placed) without over-confirming.
When something can't be done (sold out, can't ship to region), explain why and offer a next step.
Empty states explain the situation and offer an action (empty cart → "Continue shopping").
Let people cancel long operations where feasible.
Load quickly; no splash/interstitial screens.
standards.threshold: ⚠ Core Web Vitals "good" thresholds not verified this pass; Theme Store floor perf ≥ 60 (verified)

standards.rule: One defined voice; tone fits the context (errors are calm, marketing can be warmer).
Action-oriented labels; descriptive link text (no bare "click here" or "read more").
One capitalisation style per element type, applied everywhere. The kit uses sentence case (LIB-17).
Multi-step flows use consistent step verbs (Continue/Next) and clear completion (Done).
Use possessives sparingly; avoid "we" in errors ("Unable to load products").
standards.threshold: Locale lint for "We're…" or "Oops" in error strings

standards.rule: Input-agnostic verbs ("select", "choose"), not "click" or "tap", in responsive UI (LIB-13).
Error messages sit next to the problem and are actionable (see FRM-05).
Hints show format examples ("name@example.com").
Plain, inclusive language: define jargon, use people-first disability language and gender-neutral copy.
All UI strings live in Shopify `locales/*.json`; no hard-coded copy in Liquid.
Collect variant choices (size, color) before express-checkout buttons can act.
Offer express checkout on product pages. Never hide or grey out platform payment buttons. Don't require account creation before purchase.
Ratings show stars plus numeric text ("4.5 out of 5, 120 reviews"). Custom rating symbols must be clear. Never prompt for reviews mid-task or repeatedly.
Accounts: explain the benefit, delay sign-in, name the auth method, make account deletion discoverable (mostly Shopify-managed).
Ask for permissions (location for pickup, notifications) only when needed, in context, with clear copy, never on load, with no misleading pre-prompts.
No launch splash or "advert" interstitials.
Teach in context. Postpone non-essential prompts (newsletter, tours). Legal consent banners excepted (LIB-25).
Offer undo for reversible destructive actions (remove from cart).
Share uses `navigator.share` where available, with a copy-link fallback.
Product video uses native controls at its original aspect ratio, with captions and no sound autoplay (ACC-14).
